newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, fearing more bombs, ups security again.
newsitem.headline: Israel, fearing more bombs, ups security again.

text.p: Israel said on Saturday it was further increasing security in its towns and cities and along lines bordering the West Bank and Gaza Strip after Wednesday's twin suicide bombing in Jerusalem.
Police spokeswoman Linda Menuhin said there had been no specific threats of more bombings but added that Israel was working on the assumption that further attacks could follow.
The two Islamic militant bombers killed 13 other people when they blew themselves up in Jerusalem's main Jewish market on Wednesday in the worst attack in Israel for more than a year.
Menuhin said the decision to step up security, already boosted following the bombings, had been taken by Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani and police chief Assaf Hefetz.
"After consultation, Mr Kahalani and the police commissioner decided to reinforce police forces in crowded areas all over the country," Menuhin said.
More checkpoints would be set up and activities by Israeli civil guards boosted "in order to foster security".

Kahalani and Hefetz had also ordered more forces to lines along the West Bank and Gaza Strip, which Israel closed off on Wednesday when it barred Palestinians from entering its territory, and urged the public to be more alert.
Menuhin said a demand for the release of all Palestinian prisoners in a leaflet claiming responsibility for Wednesday's attack had been one consideration in Saturday's security move.

The leaflet, issued in the name of the militant Islamic movement Hamas on Wednesday night, set deadline of nine p.m. (1800 GMT) on Sunday for the demand to be met without saying what would happen if Israel ignored it.
Israeli officials say they are not certain the leaflet is authentic. A Hamas leaflet issued on Friday praised the suicide bombers but did not claim responsibility or repeat the ultimatum.
Islamic militants opposed to Israel's existence and the PLO's interim peace deals with the Jewish state have in the past carried out suicide bombings in waves.
Wednesday's twin blasts were the first since March and the deadliest since 57 people were killed in a series of suicide attacks in February and March 1996.
